description: "Gather or refresh project design context (users, jobs, tone, references, anti-references, accessibility) and persist it to docs/design-context.md. Scans the repo first and asks only for missing sections."
---

# Design-Context Onboarding

You are gathering the project's design context so that frontend workflows have a
stable, shared reference for every prompt that follows. The output is
`docs/design-context.md`.

## Step 1 — Inspect current context

1. Check whether `docs/design-context.md` exists.
   - If it exists, read it now and note which of the 7 sections below are
     already populated with real content (not placeholder text).
   - If it does not exist, all sections are missing.
2. Scan the repo for any existing design signals:
   - `README.md` — product description, target audience mentions
   - `docs/` — any architecture or product documents
   - `src/` — UI component names, any hardcoded copy
   - `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — project purpose and tech stack
3. Pre-fill what you can infer from the scan. These are starting drafts, not
   final values — the user will confirm or refine them.

## Step 2 — Ask only for missing sections

For each of the 7 sections listed below, check whether the content is already
populated in the existing file (or inferable from the scan). Ask the user **only
about sections that are missing or ambiguous**. Do not ask about sections that
are already complete.

Group the questions to minimize interruptions: batch all missing sections into a
single conversation turn if possible.

### The 7 sections

1. **Users** — Who are they? What device, context, and technical level? What
   emotional state do they bring to the product?

2. **Jobs** — What core tasks do users come to complete? What is the emotional
   goal underneath each task (e.g., "feel in control", "look competent to my
   team")?

3. **Tone** — Brand personality in 3 words. Formal or conversational? Warm or
   clinical? Any words or phrases to avoid?

4. **References** — 2–5 sites, apps, or design systems that capture the right
   feel. For each: what specifically is worth borrowing (motion, density, color
   approach, copy style)?

5. **Anti-references** — 1–3 sites or apps that represent what this UI must
   NOT look like. For each: what specifically to avoid.

6. **Accessibility** — Target WCAG level (A, AA, AAA). Any known user
   populations that need reduced-motion, high-contrast, or screen-reader
   support? Any color-blindness accommodations?

7. **Design Principles** — 3–5 product-specific rules that override generic
   best practice when they conflict. These emerge from the answers above and
   from the frontend-design skill (see
   `.github/skills/frontend-design/SKILL.md` for guidance on deriving
   principles from values, tone, and constraints).

## Step 3 — Write docs/design-context.md

After gathering all answers, write or update `docs/design-context.md` with this
structure. Keep the section headings and order exactly as shown — downstream
prompts (#944 audit, #945 normalize, #946 polish) reference this file by section
name.

```markdown
# Design Context

> Generated by the design-context prompt. Update by running `/design-context` again.

## Users

{who they are, device/context, technical level, emotional state}

## Jobs

{core tasks and the emotional goals underneath each}

## Tone

{3-word brand personality; formal/conversational; words to avoid}

## References

{2–5 sites/apps with notes on what specifically to borrow}

## Anti-References

{1–3 sites/apps with notes on what specifically to avoid}

## Accessibility

{WCAG level; reduced-motion / high-contrast / screen-reader needs; color-blindness notes}

## Design Principles

{3–5 product-specific rules, derived from the above + frontend-design skill guidance}
```

## Rules

- Do **not** ask the user to edit `.github/copilot-instructions.md` or any
  provider-config file.
- Do **not** modify any file other than `docs/design-context.md`.
- Preserve any existing content in a section — only append or refine, never
  silently delete user-supplied content.
- If all 7 sections are already populated and complete, confirm this to the user
  and offer to refine any section they want to revisit.
